From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Price <alex.price@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: context window & latency impact (follow-up)

Hi Samira / Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap plus a few follow-ups we promised to capture so we can size a realistic PoC: 

Summary of the ask we heard:
- Target latency: p95 ~200-300ms (you said 250ms is the internal goal)
- Throughput baseline: ~300 requests/sec during peak windows
- Concurrency: expected typical concurrent sessions ~6-8
- Streaming: yes — need streaming/token-by-token responses for user experience on long generations
- Context window: some flows will include very long context (up to ~32k tokens) for doc-heavy use cases; most API calls are ~2k tokens of input + 1-2k tokens output

Key perf implications we discussed (high level):
- Context window size dramatically increases per-token compute and KV memory; 32k inputs will increase latency vs 4k by ~X-3X depending on architecture and batching.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for long outputs but does not reduce total compute; it helps UX for early tokens.
- Concurrency and batching tradeoffs: larger batching helps throughput and cost but increases tail latency for single-user interactive flows.

Requests / next steps for the PoC sizing:
1) Can you confirm expected distribution of payload sizes (typical, 90th, max) — i.e., average input tokens, average output tokens, and worst-case input+output tokens? If you can attach a small sample (anonymized) payload set that helps.
2) Confirm whether streaming is mandatory for all interactive endpoints or only for a subset.
3) Fill out the attached SLO worksheet (finco-slo-metrics.xlsx) with traffic shape and peak concurrency windows — we'll use that to pick model variants and dedicated capacity.

Attached: redwood-inference-latency-profile.pdf (latency model walkthrough) and our SLO checklist.

I'll loop in our infra and runtime engineers (cc'd to follow) after you send the sample payload/worksheet. Planning note: if you need consistent p95 under 300ms at 32k context we will likely recommend a dedicated pool and prioritized routing. For initial PoC we can start with a 4k/8k context variant to baseline behavior.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0182

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary, that looks right. A few clarifications and answers below.

Confirmed SLO targets:
- p95 latency: 250ms target for interactive sessions (we understand this is tight for very long context windows)
- Throughput: peak ~300 req/s, sustained ~150 req/s outside peak
- Concurrency: typical 6-8, but spike tests should allow up to 12 concurrent sessions
- Streaming: required for the primary interactive workflow (document Q&A). Batch/asynchronous endpoints can be non-streaming.

Payload distribution (rough):
- Typical: input 1.8k tokens, output 500-800 tokens
- 90th pct: input 8k tokens, output 1k tokens
- Max (rare): input up to 32k tokens, output up to 4k tokens (document summarization flow)

I've attached an anonymized sample of 200 request headers/payload sizes and the completed SLO worksheet. Also sharing a temporary S3 link with representative files: https://s3.amazonaws.com/finco-samples/contract-queries.csv

Constraints/notes:
- We cannot truncate the first-pass context for the summarization flow; we need semantic chunking + retrieval to be evaluated.
- Cost is a factor, so if you can show throughput/lambda of different quantization variants that helps procurement.

Attaching: finco-slo-metrics.xlsx (completed)

Thanks —
Samira Khan
Head of ML Platform, FinCo
samira.khan@finco.com

Engineering asks:

3) Consider design mitigations: streaming partial responses, KV cache for repeated prefixes, hybrid retrieval + chunking for summarization (semantic chunking), and model fallback to smaller context with retrieval.

Plan to sync Wed EOD for initial numbers so we can include them in a PoC SOW for FinCo (target delivery Thu).

Hi Samira / Alex —

Appreciate the completed worksheet and sample payloads — that was very helpful. Based on the team's initial run (internal microbenchmarks + traffic shaping) here is a pragmatic PoC plan and mutual action items: 

PoC objective: baseline latency/throughput behavior across small (<=4k), medium (~8k), and large (~32k) contexts and validate streaming UX and retrieval-chunking for summarization flows.

Proposed technical configuration:
- Streaming: enabled for interactive endpoints (document Q&A)
- Max response tokens: 4096 for interactive; SOW will include test cases up to 4k output
- Concurrency target for PoC: 8 concurrent sessions (we will also run spike test to 12)
- Model variants for testing:
  * Variant A: 8k optimized (quantized kernel) — expect p95 ~120-220ms for <=4k tokens under light batching
  * Variant B: 32k full-attention — expect p95 ~400-800ms for worst-case 32k inputs (depends on batching); streaming start times better but total completion longer

Preliminary recommendations:
- For interactive UX with strict p95 250ms, target <=4k active context in Dedicated pools; use retrieval/chunking for larger doc flows.
- Use streaming to improve perceived latency for long outputs; show FinCo comparison charts for cost/latency of quantized 8k vs full 32k in the SOW.

Mutual action plan (timeline):
1) Redwood to deliver PoC SOW + cluster sizing + cost bands by EOD Thu (link to SOW draft: https://hubspot.redwood/record/FINCO-12345). (Owner: Marissa)
2) FinCo to approve SOW and provide limited test accounts + sample dataset access (Owner: Samira) — target Mon next week
3) Redwood infra to run baseline perf tests across three variants and report results (Owner: Dev) — target week 2 of PoC
4) Finalize recommendations for Dedicated sizing if SLA required (Owner: Rishi)

Next steps: I'll send the SOW draft and an invite for a 30-min kick-off once Dev and Rishi post initial numbers. If FinCo can sign the SOW (DocuSign link included) we can start cluster provisioning within 3 business days.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
